text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me if you have noticed any swollen lymph nodes in your neck, armpits, or groin, or if you've had any unintended weight loss? Also, are the bruises appearing spontaneously without any specific injury?

text: 4-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing generalized fatigue and easy bruising for 3 weeks. Over the past week, she has developed a fever and severe leg pain that wakes her up at night.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are the bruises widespread, and have you noticed any small red or purple spots on her skin that look like pinpricks? Also, does the leg pain seem to be centered in her bones or joints?

text: My main symptom is Generalized fatigue and easy bruising. I also have Fever, Severe leg pain that disturbs sleep.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you recall seeing any tiny red or purple pinprick-like spots on her skin, and has she mentioned feeling short of breath or having frequent infections lately?

text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count: Hemoglobin 10.1 g/dL, Leukocyte Count 63,000/mm3 (elevated), Platelet Count 27,000/mm3 (decreased). Note: Bone Marrow Aspirate findings also available: Predominantly immature cells positive for CD10, CD19, and TdT.

speaker: Doctor
text: The blood work shows a very high white blood cell count and low platelets, which explains the bruising and fatigue. The bone marrow results confirm the presence of immature cells, which is consistent with Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL). DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia
